title: fix: identify slow session subscription warnings
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slow `sessions.subscribe` snapshots were logged with `operation: "sessions.list"`, misattributing subscription work when investigating Gateway latency.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish slow list requests from slow subscription snapshots in warning logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared diagnostic record already carries the original request operation. Remove the warning sink's fixed override and document that both snapshot paths use the existing `slow session list` message. Thresholds, trace handling, counters, payload privacy and responses stay unchanged.

## Evidence

The regression uses the real session handlers and isolated SQLite state. Before the fix, only the subscription warning's operation disagreed with its diagnostic event. The refreshed branch passes all 21 focused diagnostic, subscription/viewer and thinking-fixture cases. The three changed files remain byte-identical to the patch that passed the complete changed-file gate and independent review through P2.

A real isolated Linux Gateway passed build, session creation without an agent turn, list readback and a nonempty subscription snapshot in [Testbox](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34970215073). All three receipts preserved the same synthetic session identity; process, listener, state and lease cleanup completed. This ran on pre-refresh commit `2fe159f`; an independent comparison of all intervening files found no changed API behavior for these fixed inputs on the refreshed head. Build/runtime execution remains attributed to `2fe159f`. No slow warning was emitted, so this is composition proof; the controlled regression above covers warning attribution.

Initial CI hit a GitHub API 500 and the inherited thinking-fixture failure fixed by [#149049](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/149049). The refreshed main base includes that repair; refreshed-head CI is tracked in the GitHub checks.
